body:
Fixes #38966
Closes #40610

## Problem

During normal startup, Lua's default `package.path` and `package.cpath` allow `require()` to load a same-named file from the current directory which allows for potential code execution by malicious plugin requests.

## Solution

Remove the exact `./?.lua` and `./?.so` templates from all package-path entries during normal startup, including worker states. Move init Lua's `arg` table 12 lines up in executor.c before package setup so `nvim -l` can retain these templates intentionally.

Add regression tests for repeated entries, `nvim -l`, and worker states.

comment_data.body:
Why is it being done this way instead of like this? As far as I can tell these behave the same.

```suggestion
if not (arg and arg[0]) then
  package.path = package.path:gsub('%./%?%.lua;', '')
  package.cpath = package.cpath:gsub('%./%?%.so;', '')
end
```
comment_data.diff_hunk:
@@ -1,3 +1,19 @@
+-- Keep default relative paths for nvim -l only.
+if not (arg and arg[0]) then
+  local function remove_cwd_template(path, pattern)
+    local result = {}
+    for entry in (path .. ';'):gmatch('(.-);') do
+      if not entry:match(pattern) then
+        result[#result + 1] = entry
+      end
+    end
+    return table.concat(result, ';')
+  end
+
+  package.path = remove_cwd_template(package.path, '^%.[/\\\\]%?%.lua$')
+  package.cpath = remove_cwd_template(package.cpath, '^%.[/\\\\]%?%.[^/\\\\;]+$')
+end

comment_data.body:
Oh right, I didn't consider Windows! `[/\\]` should work. Good catch with `.so` being platform dependent too.

Note that you don't need to escape `\` twice since `%` is the pattern escape character in lua, not `\`.

(You can also forgo escaping `\` at all if you use `[[...]]` strings instead of `'...'` strings.)

comment_regular_data.body: This was already discussed in https://github.com/neovim/neovim/pull/41794#issuecomment-5593894034 so this PR is a followup to that
(would have been helpful to mention this then, just as a general note.)

I'm sorry I'm trying to get into contributing. the code itself was llm generated but I did thoroughly check it, I really believe this is a worthwhile fix, though, sorry if this is more hassle than it's worth I can stop if it's the case. 

The code did pass all repo tests initially and I tried running github actions as to not be flagged in the autochecker as the previous pr, though last run still failed on: Ubuntu ASan/Clang functional tests. I'm not sure how I can set this up so it actually flags all issues.

It's all good, the mistake was mine -- I was not aware that there's a history to this and it's not just a random low-effort drive-by PR (which have sadly become all too frequent across Github).

And tests can be flakey; let's see how this one turns up, then we can look at the output.

With this implementation, `./?.lua;` will still not be added back correctly to threads when in `-l` mode, like in #40610. At least `package.path` is only being set in one place with this solution, so it is less janky then my impl.

Repo: run `nvim -l - <<<'vim.uv.new_thread({}, function() print(package.path) end):join()'` and notice that `./?.lua;` is not included in `package.path`.

I pushed the changes described in my latest comment. the lua-script state is now propagated to worker threads, and the package-path patterns handle both unix and windows path separators and platform-dependent C modules. 

the build and relevant tests pass; the unit suite also passes. and again this 01 autochecker issue which I don't know what to do about.
